_comment: Works the Linux executable carries that are not pinned inputs of their own: the
system libraries Nuitka copies beside the extension modules that link them, from
the Ubuntu 22.04 compile image, and the GCC runtime linked into opengrep-core.
Each entry names the package it comes from; the platform report in the release
lists the exact images. Shared conclusions come from ../determinations.json.

python-runtime/openssl.basis: libssl.so.3 and libcrypto.so.3 in the distribution come from Ubuntu 22.04's libssl3 package, OpenSSL 3.0.2
python-runtime/openssl.note: Reaches the executable whenever Nuitka follows the ssl import, which requests and urllib3 force.

python-runtime/libffi.basis: libffi.so.8 in the distribution comes from Ubuntu 22.04's libffi8 package, libffi 3.4.2

python-runtime/xz.basis: liblzma.so.5 in the distribution comes from Ubuntu 22.04's liblzma5 package, xz 5.2.5, whose liblzma is in the public domain

python-runtime/bzip2.basis: libbz2.so.1.0 in the distribution comes from Ubuntu 22.04's libbz2-1.0 package, bzip2 1.0.8

python-runtime/sqlite.basis: libsqlite3.so.0 in the distribution comes from Ubuntu 22.04's libsqlite3-0 package, SQLite 3.37.2
python-runtime/sqlite.note: peewee pulls sqlite3 into the import graph.

python-runtime/libuuid.basis: libuuid.so.1 in the distribution comes from Ubuntu 22.04's libuuid1 package, util-linux 2.37.2, whose libuuid is BSD-3-Clause

native/gcc-runtime.basis: opengrep-core links libstdc++ and libgcc statically from Ubuntu 22.04's GCC 11; the GCC Runtime Library Exception lets the compiled engine carry them under its own terms
